summary: Mary Haas was a linguist who studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University under Edward Sapir. She spent her career at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1941 to 1977.
Mary Jaksch works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and trained under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Michigan, Harvard, NYU, and Columbia University. She served at the US Department of State (1951–1958) and the National Museum of African Art (1971–1978).
Marybeth White is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned an honors degree at York University and pursued doctoral studies at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).
Maryla Falk was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held an academic post at the University of Warsaw from circa 1931 to 1939 and became a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1974.

Marylin M. Rhie was a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She served as a professor at Smith College from circa 1974 to 2013.

Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees, including a doctorate, at Kyoto University. He held positions at Kyoto University (1968, 1981–1993) and Otani University (circa 1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta. His career included long service at Kyoto University (1961–1988) and a professorship at Osaka Gakuin University (1989).

Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

Masaaki Noni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts as assistant professor (attested 2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.

Masaaki Sugiyama was a historian and scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (circa 1970–1978) and taught at Kyoto Women's University from circa 1983 to 1992.
Masaaki Tsuchiya is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kokugakuin University. He held an appointment at Senshu University around 1998.

Masaharu Anesaki was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University under Friedrich Max Müller, Paul Deussen, and others. He served as professor and library director at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai is a Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology scholar who earned his doctorate from Tokyo University of Education. He held appointments at Ibaraki University and the University of Tsukuba, along with numerous international visiting professorships.

Masahide Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Nagoya University and SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at Koyasan University, Nagoya University, and Kanazawa University.
Masahiro Asada is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University and served there as an assistant professor (attested 1987).

Masahiro Inami is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University. He held academic posts at Tokyo Gakugei University from circa 1994 and circa 2008.

Masahiro Kusunoki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University. He later served as chair professor of religious studies and history of religion at Tohoku University from circa 1974 to 1985.

Masahiro Shimoda is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his BA, MA, and doctorate at the University of Tokyo, also studying at the University of Delhi. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and Musashino University.
Masahiro Takano is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University and served there as a librarian (attested 1995).
